p: Rodes attacks. O'Neal's brigade miscarries — O'Neal does not lead in person, keeps one regiment back without orders. Iverson's brigade advances in PERFECT ALIGNMENT without skirmishers toward Oak Ridge stone wall.

IVERSON'S PITS. Baxter's Union brigade (behind stone wall) fires simultaneous volley into Iverson's flank at close range. Approximately 500 Confederates shot down in minutes. Men fall in rows — their graves visible as depressions today. Iverson reportedly does not lead the charge.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (Oak Ridge stone wall)

p: Daniel's Confederate brigade attacks south of Iverson toward the Railroad Cut area. Ramseur's brigade waits to exploit any opening. O'Neal's repulsed regiments reorganize.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (Oak Ridge / Railroad Cut south)

p: GORDON'S FLANK ATTACK. Early's division arrives on York Road northeast of town. Gordon's brigade sweeps wide around the Union XI Corps right flank, hitting Barlow's position on Barlow's Knoll from the east. Doles's brigade simultaneously attacks north of town.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (Barlow's Knoll / north of Gettysburg)

p: Barlow's Knoll overwhelmed. Barlow severely wounded — left for dead on the knoll. Gordon personally brings him water, believing him dying. Wilkeson's Union battery destroyed on the knoll. Hays's and Avery's brigades advance south toward town.
XI Corps collapses. Barlow's and Schurz's divisions broken and streaming south through Gettysburg streets. Coster's brigade sent north to cover the retreat — trapped in the brickyard disaster.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (North of Gettysburg / town streets)

p: Coster's brigade caught from three sides in brickyard north of town — 566 casualties in minutes. 134th NY, 154th NY, 27th PA, 73rd PA nearly destroyed as organized units.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (Brickyard north of Gettysburg)

p: I Corps right flank (Robinson) crumbling under Oak Hill artillery and Daniel's brigade pressure. Paul's brigade commander Paul blinded — four successive commanders wounded. 16th Maine ordered to stay as sacrifice regiment covering the retreat.

Seminary Ridge fighting begins. Pender's Confederate division arrives and attacks I Corps position. Perrin's South Carolina brigade drives through the Lutheran Seminary grounds. Scales's brigade devastated — 66% casualties.
Schimmelfennig cut off during retreat — hides in a pigpen on Baltimore Street. Von Amsberg assumes XI Corps brigade command. I Corps remnants retreating through town.

Dilger's battery (Battery I, 1st Ohio) fights rearguard action THROUGH GETTYSBURG'S STREETS — the only artillery to fight in the town itself. Engages Confederate infantry at close range on Stratton Street and Washington Street.
Union forces rally on Cemetery Hill. Howard had wisely positioned a reserve (von Steinwehr's division) here from the start. Hancock arrives from Meade — takes command and organizes the defense.
Hancock's energy and presence stabilized the Union position when everything seemed lost.

p: LEE'S DISCRETIONARY ORDER TO EWELL: 'take Cemetery Hill if practicable.' Ewell looks at the hill, considers Johnson's division not yet arrived, decides it is not practicable. Does not order the attack.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 1 (Cemetery Hill / Gettysburg town)

p: Ewell's decision not to attack Cemetery Hill July 1 evening is one of the most debated command decisions of the war. Jackson would likely have attacked.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)

p: Heth and Hill confer. Hill insists it is only Pennsylvania militia in Gettysburg. Heth asks permission to advance — Hill gives approval. The battle that neither army planned begins.
